subject: B
topic: Rapid mixed revision & weak-area drill — GK India

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Brahmaputra River enters India through which state?
questions.explanation: 'Arunachal Pradesh' is correct — the Brahmaputra (known as Siang/Dihang) enters India from Tibet through Arunachal Pradesh before flowing into Assam. 'Assam' is wrong — the river flows through Assam but enters India via Arunachal Pradesh. 'West Bengal' is wrong — the river flows through West Bengal (as Padma) only after leaving Assam and entering Bangladesh. 'Meghalaya' is wrong — the Brahmaputra does not enter India through Meghalaya.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India:

(i) GST was implemented on 1 July 2017.
(ii) It replaced multiple indirect taxes like excise duty, service tax, and VAT.
(iii) The GST Council is chaired by the Prime Minister of India.
(iv) GST is a destination-based consumption tax.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — GST was rolled out on 1 July 2017. (ii) is correct — GST subsumed excise duty, service tax, VAT, and other indirect taxes. (iv) is correct — GST is a destination-based tax levied where goods/services are consumed. (iii) is wrong — the GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, not the Prime Minister.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Thar Desert receives less than 25 cm of annual rainfall.
Reason (R): The Thar Desert lies in the rain shadow region of the Aravalli Hills, which run parallel to the moisture-bearing south-west monsoon winds.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the western part of the Thar Desert receives less than 25 cm rainfall annually. (R) is correct — the Aravalli Hills run parallel (NE-SW) to the monsoon winds rather than perpendicular, failing to block them effectively, leaving the area dry. (R) explains (A) because the Aravallis' parallel orientation to monsoon winds is a key reason for low rainfall. Option 2 is wrong because R provides a correct causal explanation. Option 3 is wrong because R is geographically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers with the states in which their source is located:

Column I:
(a) Godavari
(b) Krishna
(c) Narmada
(d) Kaveri

Column II:
(i) Madhya Pradesh
(ii) Maharashtra
(iii) Karnataka
(iv) Maharashtra

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(ii) is correct — Godavari originates near Nashik in Maharashtra (Trimbakeshwar). (b)-(iv) is correct — Krishna originates at Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra. (c)-(i) is correct — Narmada originates at Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh. (d)-(iii) is correct — Kaveri originates at Talakaveri in Kodagu district, Karnataka. The other options incorrectly assign rivers to wrong source states.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Swachh Bharat Mission' was launched on which date?
questions.explanation: '2 October 2014' is correct — the Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on Gandhi Jayanti (2 October) 2014. '15 August 2014' is wrong — the campaign was announced on Independence Day 2014 but formally launched on 2 October. '26 January 2015' is wrong — this is Republic Day 2015, not the launch date. '2 October 2015' is wrong — the mission was launched in 2014, not 2015.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Fundamental Duties under Article 51A of the Indian Constitution?

(i) To abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and National Anthem.
(ii) To vote in every election.
(iii) To protect and improve the natural environment.
(iv) To develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Art. 51A(a) mandates respecting the Constitution, Flag, and Anthem. (iii) is correct — Art. 51A(g) mandates protecting forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife. (iv) is correct — Art. 51A(h) mandates developing scientific temper and inquiry. (ii) is wrong — there is no Fundamental Duty to vote; voting is a legal right, not listed under Article 51A.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Planning Commission of India was replaced by __________ in 2015.
questions.explanation: 'NITI Aayog' is correct — the National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog) replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015. 'Finance Commission' is wrong — it is a constitutional body for revenue distribution, not a replacement for the Planning Commission. 'National Development Council' is wrong — NDC worked alongside the Planning Commission but did not replace it. 'NABARD' is wrong — it is the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, unrelated to planning.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Parliament:

(i) The Rajya Sabha has a maximum strength of 250 members.
(ii) Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
(iii) The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
(iv) The Lok Sabha can have a maximum strength of 552 members.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Rajya Sabha has a maximum of 250 members (238 elected + 12 nominated). (ii) is correct — Money Bills can only originate in the Lok Sabha (Article 109). (iii) is correct — the Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Article 64). (iv) is correct — Lok Sabha has a maximum strength of 552 (530 from states + 20 from UTs + 2 nominated Anglo-Indians, though the nomination provision expired in 2020, the constitutional maximum remains 552).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who among the following was the first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold medal?
questions.explanation: 'Abhinav Bindra' is correct — he won India's first individual Olympic gold medal in the 10m Air Rifle event at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. 'Neeraj Chopra' is wrong — he won gold in javelin at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (2021), not the first. 'Sushil Kumar' is wrong — he won bronze (2008) and silver (2012) in wrestling, never gold. 'Karnam Malleswari' is wrong — she won a bronze in weightlifting at the 2000 Sydney Olympics.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is called a 'quasi-federal' state.
Reason (R): The Indian Constitution has features of both a federal and a unitary system, with a strong central government.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — scholars like K.C. Wheare describe India as 'quasi-federal' due to its mixed character. (R) is correct — India has federal features (division of powers, written constitution) but also unitary features (single citizenship, emergency provisions, strong centre). (R) explains (A) because the combination of federal and unitary features is precisely why India is termed quasi-federal. Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains A. Option 3 is wrong because R is accurate. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Khajuraho Group of Monuments, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was built by which dynasty?
questions.explanation: 'Chandela dynasty' is correct — the Khajuraho temples in Madhya Pradesh were built by the Chandela rulers between 950–1050 CE. 'Chola dynasty' is wrong — the Cholas built temples in Tamil Nadu (e.g., Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur). 'Pallava dynasty' is wrong — they built temples at Mahabalipuram in Tamil Nadu. 'Rashtrakuta dynasty' is wrong — they built the Kailasa Temple at Ellora in Maharashtra.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Five Year Plans with their primary focus:

Column I:
(a) First Five Year Plan (1951–56)
(b) Second Five Year Plan (1956–61)
(c) Fourth Five Year Plan (1969–74)
(d) Eighth Five Year Plan (1992–97)

Column II:
(i) Human resource development and liberalization
(ii) Agriculture and irrigation
(iii) Industrialization (Mahalanobis Model)
(iv) Growth with stability (Green Revolution era)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(ii) is correct — the First Plan focused on agriculture, irrigation, and dam projects. (b)-(iii) is correct — the Second Plan (Mahalanobis Model) emphasized rapid industrialization. (c)-(iv) is correct — the Fourth Plan aimed at 'growth with stability', coinciding with Green Revolution success. (d)-(i) is correct — the Eighth Plan focused on human development and came after the 1991 liberalization. The other options misattribute plan priorities.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Right to Education' was made a Fundamental Right under which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: '86th Amendment' is correct — the 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 a Fundamental Right. '73rd Amendment' is wrong — it deals with Panchayati Raj institutions. '91st Amendment' is wrong — it restricts the size of the Council of Ministers. '44th Amendment' is wrong — it dealt with restoring fundamental rights curtailed during the Emergency.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following statements about India's space programme are correct?

(i) ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 successfully soft-landed on the Moon's south pole region in 2023.
(ii) Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) made India the first country to reach Mars orbit in its first attempt.
(iii) ISRO was founded in 1969 with Dr. Vikram Sarabhai as its first chairman.
(iv) India's first satellite, Aryabhata, was launched in 1985.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander touched down near the Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023. (ii) is correct — India's MOM reached Mars orbit in September 2014 on its maiden attempt. (iii) is correct — ISRO was established on 15 August 1969 under Dr. Vikram Sarabhai. (iv) is wrong — Aryabhata was launched on 19 April 1975 (by a Soviet rocket), not 1985.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Digital India' programme was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: '2015' is correct — the Digital India programme was launched on 1 July 2015 to transform India into a digitally empowered society. '2014' is wrong — the NDA government took office in May 2014 but Digital India was formally launched in 2015. '2016' is wrong — it is one year after the actual launch. '2017' is wrong — by 2017, Digital India was already operational for two years.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:

(i) It is a multi-member body with a Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.
(ii) The CEC can only be removed through impeachment similar to a Supreme Court judge.
(iii) It was established under Article 324 of the Constitution.
(iv) It conducts elections for the President and Vice President of India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — since 1993, the ECI has been a three-member body (CEC + 2 ECs). (ii) is correct — the CEC can only be removed by the same procedure as a Supreme Court judge (address by Parliament). (iii) is correct — Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the ECI. (iv) is correct — the ECI conducts elections for the President, Vice President, Parliament, and State Legislatures.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indian monsoon is described as 'burst' rather than 'onset' in meteorological terms because of its sudden arrival.
Reason (R): The monsoon winds arrive with a sudden increase in rainfall over a very short period, unlike gradual seasonal changes in temperate climates.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — meteorologists use 'burst of monsoon' to describe its sudden dramatic arrival over Kerala around June 1. (R) is correct — the monsoon arrives with a rapid surge of moisture-laden winds causing heavy rainfall within days, unlike gradual temperate-zone transitions. (R) explains (A) because the suddenness described in R is exactly what defines the 'burst'. Option 2 is wrong because R gives the direct reason for using 'burst'. Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Param Vir Chakra' is India's highest wartime gallantry award. Who was the first recipient?
questions.explanation: 'Major Somnath Sharma' is correct — he was posthumously awarded the first Param Vir Chakra for his bravery in the 1947 Kashmir operations at Badgam. 'Lance Naik Albert Ekka' is wrong — he received the PVC during the 1971 Indo-Pak War. 'Captain Vikram Batra' is wrong — he received the PVC during the 1999 Kargil War. 'Subedar Joginder Singh' is wrong — he received the PVC during the 1962 Sino-Indian War.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The minimum age to be elected as a member of the Rajya Sabha is __________ years.
questions.explanation: '30' is correct — Article 84 of the Constitution prescribes a minimum age of 30 years for Rajya Sabha membership. '25' is wrong — 25 is the minimum age for Lok Sabha membership. '35' is wrong — 35 is the minimum age for the office of the President of India. '21' is wrong — 21 was the earlier voting age (now 18) and is not relevant to Rajya Sabha eligibility.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs of states and their official languages are correctly matched?

(i) Tamil Nadu — Tamil
(ii) Gujarat — Gujarati
(iii) Odisha — Bengali
(iv) Andhra Pradesh — Telugu

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Tamil is the official language of Tamil Nadu. (ii) is correct — Gujarati is the official language of Gujarat. (iv) is correct — Telugu is the official language of Andhra Pradesh. (iii) is wrong — the official language of Odisha is Odia (Oriya), not Bengali. Bengali is the official language of West Bengal.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) was modelled on which international project?
questions.explanation: 'Tennessee Valley Authority (USA)' is correct — the DVC, established in 1948, was modelled on the TVA for integrated river basin development combining flood control, irrigation, and power generation. 'Aswan Dam Project' is wrong — it is an Egyptian project on the Nile, not a model for DVC. 'Three Gorges Dam' is wrong — it was completed in 2006 in China, decades after DVC's establishment. 'Hoover Dam Project' is wrong — it is a single dam on the Colorado River, not a valley authority model.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following national parks with the states they are located in:

Column I:
(a) Jim Corbett National Park
(b) Kaziranga National Park
(c) Ranthambore National Park
(d) Periyar National Park

Column II:
(i) Rajasthan
(ii) Uttarakhand
(iii) Kerala
(iv) Assam

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(ii) is correct — Jim Corbett NP is in Uttarakhand (India's first national park, est. 1936). (b)-(iv) is correct — Kaziranga NP, famous for one-horned rhinos, is in Assam. (c)-(i) is correct — Ranthambore NP, known for tigers, is in Rajasthan. (d)-(iii) is correct — Periyar NP, known for elephants, is in Kerala. The other options incorrectly pair parks with states.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The concept of 'Directive Principles of State Policy' in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of:
questions.explanation: 'Ireland' is correct — the DPSP (Part IV, Articles 36–51) was borrowed from the Irish Constitution (1937). 'USA' is wrong — India borrowed the Bill of Rights concept and judicial review from the US. 'UK' is wrong — from the UK, India borrowed parliamentary government and the rule of law. 'France' is wrong — from France, India borrowed the ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity in the Preamble.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows India's foreign trade figures (in billion USD):

Year 2020–21 → Exports: 292, Imports: 394
Year 2021–22 → Exports: 422, Imports: 613
Year 2022–23 → Exports: 451, Imports: 714

In which year was the trade deficit (Imports – Exports) the highest?
questions.explanation: Trade deficits: 2020–21: 394–292 = 102 billion USD. 2021–22: 613–422 = 191 billion USD. 2022–23: 714–451 = 263 billion USD. The highest deficit is in 2022–23 (263 billion). '2021–22' is wrong — deficit was 191 billion, lower than 2022–23. '2020–21' is wrong — deficit was only 102 billion. 'All years had equal deficit' is wrong — the deficits clearly differ across years.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about SAARC:

(i) SAARC was established in 1985 with its secretariat in Kathmandu, Nepal.
(ii) India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, and Afghanistan are its members.
(iii) SAARC has 10 member nations.
(iv) The first SAARC summit was held in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — SAARC was established on 8 December 1985 with its secretariat in Kathmandu. (ii) is correct — SAARC has 8 members (the seven founding members + Afghanistan, which joined in 2007). (iv) is correct — the first SAARC summit was held in Dhaka in December 1985. (iii) is wrong — SAARC has 8 member nations, not 10.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India's textile industry is one of the oldest industries and a major foreign exchange earner.
Reason (R): India is the world's largest producer of jute and the second-largest producer of silk.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — textiles are among India's oldest industries and a major forex earner (contributing ~11% of export earnings). (R) is correct — India is the largest jute producer and second-largest silk producer globally. However, (R) does not explain (A) because India's textile industry earns forex primarily through cotton textiles and garment exports, not specifically jute or silk. Option 1 (Both correct, R not explaining A) is the right choice. Option 2 is wrong because R doesn't causally explain A. Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the division of powers between the Union and States?
questions.explanation: 'Seventh Schedule' is correct — it contains three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List, dividing legislative powers. 'Eighth Schedule' is wrong — it lists the recognized official languages of India. 'Ninth Schedule' is wrong — it contains laws that cannot be challenged in court (added by the 1st Amendment). 'Sixth Schedule' is wrong — it deals with administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly paired (Scheme — Year of Launch)?

(i) Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana — 2014
(ii) Beti Bachao Beti Padhao — 2015
(iii) Ujjwala Yojana — 2016
(iv) Skill India Mission — 2018

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014. (ii) is correct — Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched on 22 January 2015. (iii) is correct — Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana was launched on 1 May 2016. (iv) is wrong — Skill India Mission was launched on 15 July 2015 (World Youth Skills Day), not 2018.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Siachen Glacier, the world's highest battlefield, is located in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: 'Karakoram Range' is correct — the Siachen Glacier (76 km long) is in the eastern Karakoram range in the region near the India-Pakistan Line of Control. 'Himalayan Range' is wrong — while broadly in the Himalayan system, Siachen is specifically in the Karakoram. 'Pir Panjal Range' is wrong — this range is in J&K but much further south and lower in elevation. 'Zanskar Range' is wrong — this range is between the Great Himalayas and the Indus Valley in Ladakh, not where Siachen is located.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following folk dances with their states:

Column I:
(a) Garba
(b) Bhangra
(c) Bihu
(d) Lavani

Column II:
(i) Punjab
(ii) Maharashtra
(iii) Gujarat
(iv) Assam

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(iii) is correct — Garba is a folk dance of Gujarat performed during Navratri. (b)-(i) is correct — Bhangra is a harvest dance of Punjab. (c)-(iv) is correct — Bihu is the folk dance of Assam associated with the Bihu festival. (d)-(ii) is correct — Lavani is a folk dance of Maharashtra known for its powerful rhythm. The other options incorrectly match dances with states.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which amendment to the Indian Constitution lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
questions.explanation: '61st Amendment' is correct — the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act (1988) lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years. '42nd Amendment' is wrong — it added 'socialist', 'secular', 'integrity' to the Preamble and made other sweeping changes in 1976. '52nd Amendment' is wrong — it dealt with the anti-defection law. '73rd Amendment' is wrong — it constitutionalized the Panchayati Raj system.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The data below shows rice production (in million tonnes) by four states:

West Bengal → 15.8
Uttar Pradesh → 14.5
Punjab → 13.2
Andhra Pradesh → 8.7

What is the approximate percentage contribution of Punjab to the total production shown?
questions.explanation: Total = 15.8 + 14.5 + 13.2 + 8.7 = 52.2 million tonnes. Punjab's share = (13.2/52.2) × 100 = 25.28% ≈ 25.3%. '30.2%' is wrong — this overstates Punjab's share significantly. '22.5%' is wrong — this understates the contribution. '28.1%' is wrong — this would require Punjab's production to be about 14.7 million tonnes.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'Fourth Estate' refers to:
questions.explanation: 'The Press/Media' is correct — 'Fourth Estate' is a term used to describe the press and news media, highlighting their role as an unofficial but powerful pillar of democracy. 'The Judiciary' is wrong — it is the third branch of government, not the Fourth Estate. 'The Executive' is wrong — it is one of the three formal branches of government. 'Civil society organizations' is wrong — while important, NGOs are not traditionally called the Fourth Estate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Reserve Bank of India (RBI):

(i) It was established in 1935 based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission.
(ii) It was nationalized in 1949.
(iii) Its headquarters is in New Delhi.
(iv) It acts as the banker to the Government of India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — RBI was established on 1 April 1935 based on the Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, 1926). (ii) is correct — RBI was nationalized on 1 January 1949. (iv) is correct — RBI functions as the banker to both the Central and State governments. (iii) is wrong — RBI's headquarters is in Mumbai (Fort area), not New Delhi.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a Navratna company?
questions.explanation: 'Reliance Industries' is correct (it is NOT a Navratna) — Reliance is a private sector company and Navratna status is given only to public sector enterprises (CPSEs). 'Bharat Electronics Limited' is wrong — BEL is a Navratna CPSE. 'Hindustan Aeronautics Limited' is wrong — HAL holds Navratna status. 'ONGC Videsh' is wrong — it is a subsidiary of ONGC (a Maharatna), but ONGC Videsh itself holds Navratna status.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) has its secretariat in:
questions.explanation: 'Ebene, Mauritius' is correct — the IORA secretariat is located in Ebene, Mauritius since its establishment. 'New Delhi, India' is wrong — while India is a member, the secretariat is not in India. 'Jakarta, Indonesia' is wrong — Jakarta hosts the ASEAN secretariat, not IORA. 'Colombo, Sri Lanka' is wrong — Sri Lanka is a member but does not host the IORA secretariat.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indian Constitution is described as a 'living document'.
Reason (R): The Constitution has been amended over 100 times since 1950, adapting to changing social and political needs.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the Indian Constitution is often called a 'living document' due to its capacity for growth and adaptation. (R) is correct — with over 100 amendments, the Constitution has continuously evolved. (R) explains (A) because the ability to be amended and adapt (demonstrated by 100+ amendments) is precisely what makes it a 'living document'. Option 2 is wrong because R is the direct evidence for calling it a living document. Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred during the tenure of which Viceroy?
questions.explanation: 'Lord Chelmsford' is correct — the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919) occurred during the viceroyalty of Lord Chelmsford (1916–1921). 'Lord Irwin' is wrong — he was Viceroy from 1926 to 1931. 'Lord Reading' is wrong — he served from 1921 to 1926. 'Lord Curzon' is wrong — he was Viceroy from 1899 to 1905 (known for the Partition of Bengal).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following correctly describes the Veto power in the United Nations Security Council?

(i) Only the five permanent members (P5) have veto power.
(ii) A single veto by any P5 member can block a substantive resolution.
(iii) The P5 members are USA, UK, France, Russia, and China.
(iv) Veto power can also be exercised in the UN General Assembly.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — only the P5 permanent members have veto power in the UNSC. (ii) is correct — a single 'no' vote from any P5 member blocks a substantive resolution. (iii) is correct — the P5 are USA, UK, France, Russia (formerly USSR), and China. (iv) is wrong — veto power exists only in the Security Council; the General Assembly operates on a majority voting system with no veto provision.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'Demographic Dividend' refers to:
options: Economic growth potential from a large working-age population relative to dependents
Government subsidies given based on population size
The total population of a country reaching a billion
Benefits from reducing the birth rate to zero
questions.correctAnswer: Economic growth potential from a large working-age population relative to dependents
questions.explanation: 'Economic growth potential from a large working-age population relative to dependents' is correct — demographic dividend occurs when the proportion of working-age people (15–64) exceeds the dependent population (children + elderly), creating potential for economic growth. 'Government subsidies based on population size' is wrong — this describes no recognized economic concept. 'Total population reaching a billion' is wrong — population size alone doesn't define a demographic dividend. 'Reducing birth rate to zero' is wrong — this would eliminate population growth entirely and is not related to demographic dividend.
